text:
When Igor Shesterkin was lost for the season in October, the Rangers' net went to a goalie with three NHL starts, all from last season. Dylan Garand has made 13 starts since, and he has been better than anyone had a right to expect: 1.7 goals saved above expected (how many fewer goals he has allowed than the shots usually produce), 31 allowed on 32.7 expected, and a 6-7-1 record behind a team that has not always helped him.

The best part of his game is the hardest part. On high-danger shots he has stopped .822 against a league .685, and that is where goalies separate. The soft spot is the opposite end: low-danger shots have beaten him a little more than average.

His run has shaped the roster. The New York Post's Mollie Walker reported James Reimer going on waivers as "next step in Joonas Korpisalo's impending return." Garand's last five starts are 1.48 goals above expected. What to watch: how the starts split once Korpisalo is back, and whether Garand's numbers make that an easy call.
headline: Dylan Garand is holding the Rangers' net together
